questions.prompt: WPF panels lay out their children in two passes. What happens in each one?
options: Arrange decides how big children want to be; Measure places them
Measure applies styles; Arrange applies data bindings
Measure asks how big children want to be; Arrange places them
Measure runs once at startup; Arrange runs only when the window is resized
questions.explanation: Panels measure and arrange their children in two layout passes: Measure (how big children want to be) and Arrange (where children are placed).

questions.prompt: A Grid has `<ColumnDefinition Width="*"/>` and `<ColumnDefinition Width="2*"/>`. How is the width shared?
options: Space is shared proportionally: the second column is twice as wide
The first column is 1 pixel wide and the second is 2 pixels wide
Both columns size to their content and the stars are ignored
The second column takes all the space and the first collapses
questions.explanation: Star sizing (`*`, `2*`) shares the remaining space proportionally; `Auto` sizes to content and a plain number is fixed pixels.

questions.prompt: In the DockPanel application shell, the final `<Grid>` has no `DockPanel.Dock` value. Where does it end up?
options: Docked at the top, because `Top` is the default `DockPanel.Dock` value
Stacked underneath the 200-wide left navigation StackPanel
Hidden, because every DockPanel child must set a dock value
Filling the remaining space, since `LastChildFill` defaults to `true`
questions.explanation: By default the last child of a DockPanel fills the remaining space (`LastChildFill=true`), which is why the main content Grid goes last after the Menu, ToolBar, StatusBar and side panel.

questions.prompt: Why is a plain StackPanel a poor host for a huge list of items?
options: It can only stack vertically, so wide items get clipped on the right
It measures children with infinite space, which defeats virtualization
It ignores the `Margin` set on its children when it arranges them
It cannot be placed inside a ScrollViewer to make it scroll
questions.explanation: StackPanel gives children infinite space in the stacking direction during measure, which is not ideal for virtualization or huge lists; use a `VirtualizingStackPanel` inside an ItemsControl instead.

questions.prompt: You have several stacked forms, each in its own Grid, and want their label columns to line up at the same width. What does the lesson suggest?
options: Wrap all the Grids in a single UniformGrid
Give every label column `Width="Auto"`
`SharedSizeGroup` on the columns, `SharedSizeScope` on the parent
Replace the Grids with StackPanels set to `Orientation="Horizontal"`
questions.explanation: Use `SharedSizeGroup` when columns across separate Grids should line up: set `SharedSizeGroup` on the column definitions and `SharedSizeScope` where the Grid is defined.

questions.prompt: You are building a calculator keypad where every button must be exactly the same size, with no row or column definitions to maintain. Which panel fits best?
options: `Canvas`
`UniformGrid`
`WrapPanel`
`DockPanel`
questions.explanation: `UniformGrid` gives each cell equal size and needs no row/column definitions, which is why the lesson uses it for a calculator keypad.
